newsitem.title: USA: Clinton signals flexibility on budget fix - aide.
newsitem.headline: Clinton signals flexibility on budget fix - aide.

text.p: President Clinton, in saying that he is willing to "take some heat" on a cost of living adjustment, is seeking to show congressional Republicans he is willing to be flexible on the issue, a senior administration official said on Monday.
Clinton told CBS News's Face the Nation program in an interview broadcast on Sunday that "If it takes some heat to do the right thing, I'll do that."

He was referring to the question of reducing the cost of living adjustment for Social Security and other programs currently based on the Consumer Price Index, which is widely believed to overstate inflation.
"It was probably not that calibrated, but he certainly wanted to indicate flexibility," the administration official, who declined to be further identified, said.

The official said Clinton wanted to "remind the other side that we are taking heat, ... (so it was) partly a little signal flare for (Senate Majority leader Trent) Lott but also a reminder that we already are (taking heat on the issue)," the official said.

In the CBS interview, Clinton indicated a willingness to consider changing the cost of living adjustment, saying: "Whatever we do must be done on the merits. I am not prepared to say to you that I am willing to get some arbitrary, completely arbitrary, political fix on the budget. But if it takes some heat to do the right thing, I'll do that."
Some congressional Democrats have been critical of such an adjustment because it would reduce benefits to the elderly and other program recipients.
